title: Roadmap Aligner: SLO Decomposition & Initiative Heatmap for Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we scale Dedicated and Private deployments, product teams are having difficulty mapping high-level SLOs to the per-route / per-model changes produced by initiatives (model swaps, batching changes, kernel selection). This causes surprise error-budget consumption and last-minute rollbacks.

Objective: Build a lightweight roadmap alignment artifact and a Console-based initiative heatmap that lets PMs/Eng/Design: (1) decompose product SLO targets into measurable route/model SLIs, (2) score each initiative for projected error-budget impact, (3) prescribe rollout gates and rollback thresholds.

Scope:
- SLO decomposition template (product -> route -> model) with recommended SLIs (p95 latency, p99 latency, token-error-rate, inference-failure-rate, tail-kv-cache-miss-rate).
- Initiative heatmap prototype in Console that projects estimated error-budget delta based on planned changes and historical SLI variability.
- Rollout gate definitions and automation suggestions (canary sizes, burn-rate triggers, auto-fallback to safe model variant).
- Integration points: telemetry (Observability team dashboards), experimentation metadata (Experiment service / A/B tags), existing rollout API in Platform.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable SLO decomposition template published in Confluence with examples for text-generation, embeddings, and reranking routes.
A Console heatmap prototype that takes planned initiatives and shows estimated error-budget impact for the next 28 days (UI mock + data sketch).
Rollout gate spec that includes numeric thresholds (canary size, % error-budget spent over window, baseline SLI regression margin) and a runbook for rollback.
Integration plan (list of data feeds + owners) that allows the heatmap to be fed by existing SLI telemetry within 2 cycles.
Stakeholder signoff from Observability, Runtime, and Solutions Engineering on scoring methodology.
notes: Scoring approach: combine sensitivity (expected SLI delta per-initiative) with exposure (queries/sec or weight of route) to estimate error-budget delta.
Trade-offs: tighter canaries reduce customer blast radius but increase rollout cycle time. We'll default to 2% traffic canary with a 30m observation window for high-impact kernels.
Data quality concern: historically p99 signals are noisy for low-traffic routes; use aggregated percentile smoothing and require >1000 requests in window to act on p99 numbers.
We will prioritize modeling for routes that account for >70% of error-budget consumption across production clusters (Hosted + Dedicated).

implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Prototype): 1 week - produce Confluence template + static Console mock that accepts CSV input for scoring.
Phase 2 (Integrate telemetry): 2 cycles - wire SLI feeds into a backend service that computes scores daily and renders the heatmap.
Phase 3 (Automation): 1 cycle - tie gating decisions to rollout API; implement opt-in auto-fallback to compatible model variant when burn-rate exceeds threshold.
Rollout timeline: soft release to internal tenants (Solutions Eng, Platform) then 2-week beta for a subset of Dedicated customers.
risks: Score accuracy risk: incorrect sensitivity estimates could mis-rank initiatives; mitigation: conservative confidence intervals and manual review flag for high-impact changes.
Operational complexity risk: additional telemetry joins could increase query cost; mitigation: pre-aggregation and sampling of SLI windows.
Behavioral risk: teams may over-rely on heatmap scores; mitigation: emphasize this as a decision-support tool and maintain human approvals for Tier-1 rollouts.
